Monte Carlo computation of posterior probability distribution - alternative

Source: R/internal_learnalt.R
dot-learnalt.Rd

Compute the posterior joint probability distribution of the variates conditional on the given data, by means of Markov-chain Monte Carlo, using the package Nimble. Alternative version that use Geyer's methods to compute ESS and MCSE, for development use.

See documentation for learn().

Usage

.learnalt(
  data,
  metadata,
  auxdata = NULL,
  outputdir = NULL,
  nsamples = 3600,
  nchains = 8,
  nsamplesperchain = 450,
  parallel = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  cleanup = TRUE,
  appendinfo = TRUE,
  valueisK = TRUE,
  subsampledata = NULL,
  prior = missing(data) || is.null(data),
  startupMCiterations = 3600,
  minMCiterations = 0,
  maxMCiterations = 9e+05,
  maxhours = +Inf,
  ncheckpoints = 12,
  maxrelMCSE = 0.04,
  minESS = 625,
  initES = 8,
  thinning = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE,
  plottraces = !cleanup,
  showKtraces = FALSE,
  showAlphatraces = FALSE,
  hyperparams = list(ncomponents = 64, minalpha = -4, maxalpha = 4, byalpha = 1, Rshapelo
    = 0.5, Rshapehi = 0.5, Rvarm1 = 3^2, Cshapelo = 0.5, Cshapehi = 0.5, Cvarm1 = 3^2,
    Dshapelo = 0.5, Dshapehi = 0.5, Dvarm1 = 3^2, Bshapelo = 1, Bshapehi = 1, Dthreshold
    = 1, tscalefactor = 4.266, Oprior = "Hadamard", Nprior = "Hadamard", avoidzeroW =
    NULL, initmethod = "datacentre", Qerror = pnorm(c(-1, 1)))
)
